meta.title: Who really said "Everyone is born a genius, but the process of living de-geniuses them"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Fuller’s idea, not his sentence. Wikiquote records a longer 1974 statement; the crisp one-liner in circulation has no source we could find.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Everyone is born a genius, but the process of living de-geniuses them'?
meta.ogDescription: The verb is Fuller’s, the sentence is not. His documented 1974 wording is longer and different, and the popular line is unsourced.

answer.label: Not Fuller’s wording — a tightened paraphrase
answer.authorDates: 1895–1983 · American architect, systems theorist and inventor
answer.sourceLine: The sentiment is squarely Fuller’s, and so is the odd verb “de-geniused.” The sentence is not. Wikiquote’s sourced entry records him stating, in 1974, “I am convinced all of humanity is born with more gifts than we know. Most are born geniuses and just get de-geniused rapidly.” The compact version people quote appears in none of its sourced entries, and we found no primary source for it.

source.excerpt: I am convinced all of humanity is born with more gifts than we know. Most are born geniuses and just get de-geniused rapidly.
trail: Wikiquote’s Buckminster Fuller page ↗ carries, among its 1970s sourced quotes, “I am convinced all of humanity is born with more gifts than we know. Most are born geniuses and just get de-geniused rapidly,” cited as a statement made in 1974, quoted in People magazine, and reprinted in Thomas T. K. Zung’s anthology at page 174.

The popular one-liner is absent from that page. We fetched the full page source and searched it for “genius”: the 1974 sentence is the only match. That is our own check of the page, not a claim Wikiquote makes.

Zung’s anthology ↗ is catalogued at the Internet Archive under St. Martin’s Press with a date of 2001, where Wikiquote cites a 2002 printing for page 174. We could not open the book to reconcile the two or to check the page, so the locator here is reported as Wikiquote’s, not confirmed as ours.
Quote Investigator, which this site defers to, has no article on this line; searches for it returned none. So there is no specialist finding to adopt, and nothing we found dates the popular wording.
source.excerptNote: This is the documented statement, which is longer and hedged (“most,” not “everyone”) where the popular version is absolute. The quotable one-liner is a later compression by an unknown hand.

source.rightsNote: We assert no rights status for the line as quoted, because we could not identify any work that contains it. Fuller’s documented 1974 statement is a separate matter and is plainly in copyright — it is decades after 1931 — with rights sitting with his estate and the publications that carried it. author.name: R. Buckminster Fuller
author.heading: About R. Buckminster Fuller
author.metaLine: 1895–1983 · American architect, systems theorist, inventor and futurist
author.bio: Richard Buckminster Fuller Jr. — who styled himself R. Buckminster Fuller in print — was an American architect, systems theorist, designer, inventor and futurist best known for popularising the geodesic dome. He published more than thirty books and coined or popularised Spaceship Earth, Dymaxion, synergetics and tensegrity. He also lectured constantly, rephrasing the same arguments in slightly different words each time — which is exactly the habit that leaves a trail of quotations nobody can pin to a page.

misattribution.heading: Often misattributed
misattribution.intro: Nobody else is claiming this line. The problem is the words: a Fuller paraphrase that hardened into a quotation and now circulates in quotation marks with his name on it.

items.why: No primary source, transcript or dated printing has been found for “Everyone is born a genius, but the process of living de-geniuses them.” Wikiquote’s sourced entry ↗ carries a longer and materially different 1974 sentence instead, and we found no specialist investigation of the short form.
Fuller really did argue that people are born gifted and then get “de-geniused” — he is documented using the verb in the 1974 statement. Only the compressed sentence in circulation is undocumented.

misattribution.truthLine: Fuller’s idea, someone else’s sentence. What he is documented saying, in 1974, is that most people “are born geniuses and just get de-geniused rapidly” — per Wikiquote’s sourced entry ↗.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Fuller’s real claim was narrower and more interesting than the poster version. He did not say everyone is a genius; he said humanity is born with more gifts than it knows, that most are born geniuses, and that the losing happens fast. The hedge is the argument: it is a claim about how much gets destroyed, not a flattering one about how special everybody is.

The paraphrase sands that off. “Everyone is born a genius” is absolute where Fuller said “most,” and “the process of living” is vague where he was pointing at something done to children by adults and institutions. It quotes better and claims less.
detailsBody: Fuller is an unusually easy author to paraphrase badly. He wrote more than thirty books in a dense, coined-vocabulary style and lectured constantly, rephrasing himself freely, so the same thought survives in many slightly different forms. That gives a tidy rewrite plenty of cover: it sounds like something he said because he said something like it, repeatedly.

What we can say is bounded. The idea is his, the verb is his, and the specific sentence in circulation is not traceable to him by anything we could reach. We have therefore not given this page a date of creation or a containing work for the popular wording, because we would have had to invent both.
context.pull: He said “most,” not “everyone” — and the hedge was the point.
